answer: Each agent’s influence can be capped by requiring a unique, scarce stake that is locked before it can vote or claim rewards, with penalties for proven double-claiming. The protocol checks that the same stake cannot back multiple identities, so copying software or minting accounts adds no weight. An attacker must acquire and immobilize real capital for every extra identity, paying opportunity cost and risking a slash; identities are cheap, but influence is not. A copper token on a ridge above a canyon is only useful if it represents that verifiable stake.
